# ViewSpec

> ViewSpec is a free, local, MIT-licensed agent-native app compiler and UI compiler: agents emit IntentBundle or AppBundle JSON, and ViewSpec compiles UI, state, reducers, shell artifacts, proof reports, HTML, React, and CompositionIR. There is no hosted service, account, API key, or paid tier.

ViewSpec lets agents describe semantic UI and app intent instead of hand-authoring DOM or state reducers. The local SDK validates `viewspec.intent.json` and `viewspec.app.json`, compiles with `DESIGN.md`, writes provenance and shell manifests, generates bounded `state_reducer.ts` artifacts for `interactive_state_v0`, and checks artifacts without SDK network calls for agentic engineering workflows.

It remains an agent-native UI compiler for IntentBundle screen work; AppBundle adds the proof story for UI plus state.

Raw HTML remains available only for importing existing HTML: `viewspec compile` auto-detects `.html` input and sanitizes, themes, and manifests it, and `viewspec check` checks the result.

## Commands

The CLI is exactly six commands:

- `viewspec init [intent|app|design] [--kind K] [--template T] [--out P] [--force] [--json]` writes a starter IntentBundle, AppBundle, or DESIGN.md.
- `viewspec compile INPUT --out DIR [--target T] [--design P] [--json]` compiles an IntentBundle, AppBundle, or imported raw HTML, auto-detected.
- `viewspec check PATH [--json]` runs fast static, provenance, and security checks on a source file or compiled artifact directory.
- `viewspec prove [SOURCE] [--out D] [--target T] [--install] [--with-shell] [--freerange] [--pretext] [--json]` compiles and verifies a source, or browser-verifies a compiled artifact, and writes a proof bundle. With no source it proves a starter.
- `viewspec studio [SOURCE] [--design P] [--port N] [--no-open] [--json]` serves a live-reloading local preview of a source file on 127.0.0.1. It rebuilds when the source or an optional DESIGN.md changes, and a failed build keeps the last good one on screen with its errors. It is a preview only: it does not generate source, collect comments or approvals, or share builds.
- `viewspec mcp [--cwd DIR] [--allow-outside-cwd] [--json]` serves the other five to a coding agent as MCP tools over stdio, confined to the working directory. It needs `pip install --pre "viewspec[agents]"`.

## Current Product Facts

- Current public SDK version: `0.4.0b1` (beta).
- Free, MIT-licensed beta SDK: `python -m pip install --pre viewspec`. Plain `python -m pip install viewspec` follows the stable channel because pip excludes prereleases by default.
- Starter proof: `viewspec prove --out .viewspec-proof` writes `.viewspec-proof/PROOF.md` for humans, `.viewspec-proof/proof_report.json` for tools, and `.viewspec-proof/support_bundle.json` for redacted local support triage; checked manifest summaries include compact style-delta counts when aesthetic profiles are present; `docs/proof-bundle.md` and https://viewspec.dev/proof-bundle/ explain status, hashes, checks, failure codes, and support bundles.
- Canonical authored-intent lifecycle: `viewspec init --out viewspec.intent.json`; edit the semantic source; `viewspec check viewspec.intent.json --json`; then `viewspec prove viewspec.intent.json --target react-tailwind-tsx --install --out .viewspec-proof --json`. The final command compiles, checks, and renders the exact artifact at canonical mobile, tablet, and desktop viewports.
- Freerange opt-in for generated `react-tailwind-app` proofs: `viewspec prove viewspec.app.json --target react-tailwind-app --install --freerange --json` pins https://github.com/chenglou/freerange as `@chenglou/freerange@0.0.1` and reports `static_analysis` plus `analyses.freerange`. It requires a user-installed stable Bun 1.x; ViewSpec never installs Bun. Its v2 contract binds every eligible state-operation occurrence to the emitted state contract, exact helpers, 100% analysis, and runtime call sites; it does not cover CSS, rendered geometry, arbitrary math, or arbitrary host applications.
- Pretext opt-in for generated `react-tailwind-app` proofs: `viewspec prove viewspec.app.json --target react-tailwind-app --install --pretext --json` pins https://github.com/chenglou/pretext as `@chenglou/pretext@0.0.8` and reports `text_layout` plus `analyses.pretext`. Its v2 protocol independently inventories every eligible checked-manifest text surface per route and viewport before checking native-DOM versus Pretext line count and overflow using named `Arial, sans-serif` at 390x844, 768x1024, and 1440x1000 in Chromium. It needs no Bun and is not general typography, canvas, visual-regression, accessibility, or arbitrary-host proof.
- Compose both with `viewspec prove viewspec.app.json --target react-tailwind-app --install --freerange --pretext --json`. A dedicated CI workflow covers healthy proofs plus real division, bounds, font, wrapping, and overflow mutation rejection on relevant changes, weekly, and by manual dispatch; this does not claim that a CI run has completed.
- Accessibility proof: `viewspec prove` runs `a11y_contrast` (fail-closed) and `a11y_names` (fail-closed; interactive controls need an author-provided accessible name). Every governed text/background pair meets size/role-scoped WCAG AA (body 4.5:1, large text and UI components 3.0:1), enumerated from the closed style vocabulary plus fixed base pairs so it provably covers every node — including the react-tailwind-tsx emitter, resolved against the browser-grounded Tailwind v4 palette. See `docs/known-limits-a11y.md`.
- Runtime LLM calls: zero in local `viewspec compile`, `viewspec check`, `viewspec prove`, and `viewspec studio`, and zero in generated artifacts.
- Agents should emit `viewspec.intent.json` for new UI and use the canonical authored-intent lifecycle above. Lower-level `viewspec compile` and `viewspec check` remain expert/debug surfaces.
- Use `viewspec init design --out DESIGN.md` when the repo does not already have a design file.
- `viewspec check` exits 0 for valid intent, 2 for user-correctable invalid intent, and 1 for environment/internal failure.
- Validation issues include severity, code, path, message, suggestion, and a bounded repair_checklist; correction prompts require full IntentBundle regeneration.
- V1 local IntentBundle caps: max 256KB JSON, 200 substrate nodes, 32 regions, 400 bindings, 64 groups, 32 motifs, 400 styles, 64 actions, 64 attrs/slots/edges per node, 200 values per slot or edge, and 64 payload bindings per action.
- V1 public SDK agent ids and object keys use only letters, digits, underscore, dot, and dash.
- AppBundle commands: `viewspec init app --out viewspec.app.json`, `viewspec init app --resource-binding fixture-readonly-v0 --out viewspec.bound.app.json`, `viewspec check viewspec.app.json --json`, `viewspec compile viewspec.app.json --out app-dist --target html-tailwind-app --json`, and `viewspec prove viewspec.app.json --out .viewspec-app-proof --with-shell --json`.
- Runnable React internal tools: `viewspec init app --template react-app --out viewspec.app.json`, replace the sample intent, then `viewspec compile viewspec.app.json --target react-tailwind-app --out app-dist`.
- AppBundle State IR demo: https://viewspec.dev/appbundle-state-ir/ shows `interactive_state_v0`, `reduceViewSpecState`, `state_replay_assertions`, `viewspec prove viewspec.app.json --with-shell`, and `state_reducer.ts` as the concrete proof surface.
- AppBundle is local-only app contract proof for multi-screen internal tools: static routes, embedded local V1 screen IntentBundles, V1 `resource_binding: "unbound_v0"` fixture context, optional V2 `fixture_readonly_v0` exact scalar visibility proofs for declared `resource_views`, optional V3 `interactive_state_v0` state/mutations/selectors/replay assertions with a pure reducer artifact, optional V4 `visibility_v0` bounded show/hide rules with baked initial visibility and a replay-proved `evaluateViewSpecVisibility` reducer export, and per-screen html-tailwind compile/check artifacts. Static Shell V0 writes a bounded local `html-tailwind-app` shell with `route_navigation: "static_shell_v0"` and no external network/embed/script surfaces. For V3 it also writes `state_reducer.ts` and `state_manifest.json`, with a generated `reduceViewSpecState` export and checked `state_replay_assertions`. For V4 it also includes the generated reducer and one bounded delegated click listener that dispatches declared mutations and toggles `hidden` on `data-visibility-rule` nodes. It does not prove runtime navigation or browser history semantics, runtime fixture data binding, live data or text rebinding, or transformed values, generate a deployable framework app, install a framework state adapter, or persist or sync state. State IR is not Redux, Zustand, CRDT, persistence, or backend generation.
- Raw HTML input is import/fallback only for existing HTML.
- Generated outputs such as `dist/index.html` and `react-output/ViewSpecView.tsx` are artifacts; edit `viewspec.intent.json` or `DESIGN.md` instead.
- Local compile targets: `html-tailwind`, `react-tsx`, `react-tailwind-tsx`, `html-tailwind-app`, and `react-tailwind-app`.
- Agents should output IntentBundle JSON, not CompositionIR, HTML, CSS, or React source for new UI.
- Agents must not call remote reference libraries by default. If the user explicitly asks for research or repo instructions configure an approved source, references may inform semantic intent only.
- Motif plugins are deterministic local `MotifPlugin` extensions that lower custom motif intent into portable `CompositionIR`; they are not dynamic filesystem discovery, remote plugin loading, or an untrusted sandbox.
- V1 public SDK motifs: table, dashboard, outline, comparison, list, form, detail, empty_state, loading_state, error_state, hero.
- V1 public SDK action kinds: select, submit, navigate, search, filter, sort, paginate, bulk_action.
- Collection actions target table/list motifs and dispatch events only; host apps own filtering, sorting, pagination, and selection state.
- V1 public SDK action target_ref is null/empty or region:id, binding:id, motif:id, or view:id.
- V1 public SDK agent binding cardinality: exactly_once.
- V1 public SDK agent group kind: ordered.
- V1 public SDK agent region layouts: stack, grid, cluster.
- V1 public SDK agent regions must form one acyclic tree rooted at view_spec.root_region.
- V1 public SDK semantic edges must reference declared substrate.nodes ids.
- V1 public SDK style targets must be explicit refs or unambiguous bare ids.
- V1 public SDK complexity_tier starts at 1, region child bounds are non-negative, and max_children is null or at least min_children.
- V1 public SDK agent style tokens must come from agent-intent-bundle.schema.json, not arbitrary CSS.
- V1 aesthetic profile tokens are deterministic art-direction handles, not CSS: aesthetic.calm_ops, aesthetic.premium_saas, aesthetic.data_dense, aesthetic.editorial_product, aesthetic.executive_review, aesthetic.brutalist, aesthetic.neon_cyber, and aesthetic.warm_organic. The homepage at https://viewspec.dev/ switches between eight compiled landing artifacts and exposes https://viewspec.dev/landing-compiled/profile-evidence.json with stable semantic ids, distinct style projection hashes, and 0 shell overrides. At most one profile may target view:{view_spec.id}; profiles may derive governed style projection, bounded layout metadata, and compact style-delta counts in checked manifest summaries, and are not pixel-perfect visual proof, accessibility certification, arbitrary host-app compatibility, or design-review approval.
- Unknown local V1 extension fields fail with UNKNOWN_FIELD instead of being ignored.
- Public facts manifest: https://viewspec.dev/public-facts.json
- Host proof assertion requirements: `assertion_requirements` reports expected `dom_count`, `style_assertion_count`, and manifest-derived `aesthetic_layout_assertion_count`, `aesthetic_profile_assertion_count`, and `grid_span_assertion_count` before observed grid column/span counts, profiled aesthetic marker/layout assertions, and action payload checks are accepted.
- Proof scope: ViewSpec prove is not pixel-perfect visual regression, accessibility certification, or arbitrary host-app certification.

## Short Description

ViewSpec is a free, local, agent-native app compiler: agents describe UI and app intent once as IntentBundle or AppBundle JSON, and ViewSpec compiles deterministic UI, state reducers, shell artifacts, and proof reports without asking agents to author DOM or state code.
